subject: general
question: Which of the following symbols represents a rheostat?

options.text: A circle with a 'V' inside it.
A zigzag line with an arrow which is drawn across it.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A zigzag line with an arrow which is drawn across it**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **rheostat** is an electrical instrument used to control **current** by varying the **resistance** in a circuit without changing the voltage source.
 
• The standard circuit symbol for a **rheostat** is a **zigzag line** (which represents resistance) with a **diagonal arrow** drawn across it or an arrow pointing down onto the zigzag. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• It functions as a **variable resistor** and is typically constructed using a resistive wire (like **manganin** or **constantan**) wrapped around an insulating ceramic core, with a sliding contact.
 
• By moving the **slider** (the arrow in the symbol), the effective length of the wire through which the current passes changes, thereby altering the total **resistance** of the circuit according to the formula **R = ρ(L/A)**.
 
• In **Ohm's Law** experiments, a **rheostat** is frequently used to adjust the current flowing through a conductor to observe the corresponding change in **potential difference**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ammeter:**
 
 
• Represented by an **'A' inside a circle**.
 
• It is a device used to measure the **electric current** in a circuit in **Amperes**.
 
• It has **low resistance** and is always connected in **series** with the circuit component. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Voltmeter:**
 
 
• Represented by a **circle with a 'V' inside it**.
 
• It is used to measure the **potential difference** (voltage) between two points in an electrical circuit.
 
• It has **high resistance** and is always connected in **parallel** across the points where the voltage is to be measured. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Fixed Resistor:**
 
 
• Represented by a simple **zigzag line**.
 
• It provides a specific, unchanging amount of **electrical resistance** to the flow of current.
 
• The unit of measurement for resistance is the **Ohm (Ω)**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Galvanometer:**
 
 
• Represented by a **'G' inside a circle**.
 
• It is an electromechanical instrument used for **detecting** and indicating the **presence and direction** of small electric currents.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Potentiometer vs. Rheostat:** While both are variable resistors, a **potentiometer** is typically used as a **voltage divider** using three terminals, whereas a **rheostat** is used to control **current** using only two terminals.
 
• **Applications:** Rheostats are used in **motor speed control**, **light dimmers**, and older **volume control** knobs in radio sets.
 
• **Ohm’s Law:** The relationship **V = IR** dictates that if **voltage (V)** is constant, increasing the **resistance (R)** using a rheostat will decrease the **current (I)**.
 
• **Safety:** When using a **rheostat** in laboratory experiments, it is vital to ensure it can handle the **wattage** or heat generated by the current to prevent damage to the component.
